name: img-tabs-standalone

frames.best_why: The first question is open with its full answer in a white block and the large photo beside it, all settled.

tagline: Picking a question on the left opens its answer beside a photo.
summary: Three bold questions stack down the left of a dark stage; choosing one outlines it in blue, drops a short answer underneath and shows a large rounded photo on the right.
appearance: A narrow left column of three heavy white question rows on near-black, the active one ringed in cobalt blue and filled deeper navy, with a white answer block hanging under it. The right half is one large rounded photo.
behaviour: Clicking a row opens its answer with a quick height fade and swaps the right-hand picture to that row's image, fading the old photo out. The blue outline stays on the chosen row until another is clicked.
demo_content: Three questions about UI and UX, illustrated with a building, a rose and mountains.
search_phrases: questions that open an answer and photo
tab list beside a large image
click a heading to expand its text
questions on the left picture on the right
use_when: A handful of detailed questions each need a short answer and an illustration next to it.
avoid_when: The rows only answer mouse clicks, and the photo box is a fixed 400 px tall, so wide images get cropped.
customise: There are no props: questions, answers and photo links sit in the tabs array in the file, and the blue outline and fixed heights are hard-coded classes.
weight_why: One photo and one expanding panel at a time, with short fades.

a11y.note: Rows are clickable divs with no tab role or tabIndex, so the switcher is mouse only; the photos do carry alt text.

issues: Rows are divs with no tabIndex or tab role, so the switcher is mouse only.
In frames 2 and 4 answer text overlaps the next row during the height change.
The second and third answers are much longer, so the left column jumps height on each switch.
polish_why: Legible split layout with a clear active outline; answers jump height and overlap mid-switch.
